CHAPTER 06 / WEBFRONT

Testing a user journey

Writing Jasmine tests and running them in a C++ application’s page.

Notation conventions

Function names, types, commands, options and filenames appear in monospace, for example describe, wf test or main.cpp. Italics introduce a term at its definition. Code blocks give the fragments to enter; the preceding text states their location and prerequisites.

The elements of a Jasmine test ↓Checking the grid format ↓Declaring the test files ↓Checking TypeScript types ↓Installing type declarations ↓Testing the project or the application ↓The example screen ↓Writing the journey test ↓Preparing the C++ application ↓Registering the test in CMake ↓Running the test and interpreting its result ↓Choosing further journeys ↓

The elements of a Jasmine test

Jasmine is a JavaScript testing library. A test describes an operation and checks the result it should produce. This chapter uses the following functions:

  • describe groups tests concerning the same behaviour.
  • it defines one test case.
  • expect checks a value or property of the result.
  • beforeAll prepares conditions shared by a suite.
  • beforeEach establishes the conditions required before each case.

An asynchronous test can use async and await to wait for a C++ reply. We shall begin with a data-format test, then test a journey in a real interface.

Checking the grid format

In the WebFront terminal, install Jasmine with wf install jasmine-core@7.0.2. Then create tests/life.spec.js in life-project.

The following test checks the packing of three cells into a byte array. It concerns the JavaScript grid representation; it does not yet check the Conway rules calculated in C++.

JAVASCRIPT / JASMINE
describe('the Life grid', () => {
    it('packs 1024 cells into 128 bytes', () => {
        const cells = new Uint8Array(32 * 32 / 8);
        for (const i of [330, 331, 332])
            cells[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7);
        expect(cells.length).toBe(128);
        expect(cells[41]).toBe(0b00011100);
    });
});

Declaring the test files

Add the following property at the root of webfront.project.json, retaining the commas required by JSON. wf init does not create this recipe.

Run wf test. Jasmine is loaded in the window and the command fails when an assertion is false. To check this behaviour, temporarily replace 128 with 127 in the test, then restore the correct value.

SOURCE
"test": {"specs": ["tests/life.spec.js"]}

Checking TypeScript types

Create tsconfig.json at the root of life-project, using the configuration below. Type checking will use the TypeScript version recorded in the lock file.

Type checking and test execution serve different purposes. The former checks the programme’s static consistency; the latter observes its runtime behaviour.

SOURCE
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "noEmit": true
  },
  "include": ["ui"]
}

Installing type declarations

The starter imports React and React DOM. Strict checking requires their type declarations as well as the TypeScript compiler. The following commands install them and run wf check.

WEBFRONT TERMINAL
wf install typescript@5.9.3 @types/react@19.3.0 @types/react-dom@19.3.0
wf check

Testing the project or the application

wf test runs the specifications declared in the development project’s manifest, using its locked jasmine-core version.

To test an existing C++ application’s page, we can also use webfront_add_jasmine_test. This helper loads Jasmine and the tests into the application’s actual page. Its normal scripts, DOM elements and C++ callbacks remain available.

This second method integrates with CTest. It requires no developer terminal, wf manifest or host JavaScript runtime, and does not depend on MCP.

The example screen

Consider a small quotation screen. The user enters a quantity and requests a calculation. The programme calls the C++ function quote.calculate and displays the returned total.

Create ui/index.html with the following contents. The button remains disabled during the call, and errors are displayed in the page. The appReady promise belongs to this example; it is not a WebFront property. Tests will use it to wait until the page has installed its handlers.

HTML / JAVASCRIPT
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Quotation</title>
<label for="quantity">Quantity</label>
<input id="quantity" type="number" value="1" min="1">
<button id="calculate" disabled>Calculate</button>
<output id="total" aria-live="polite"></output>
<p id="status" role="status"></p>
<script src="/WebFront.js"></script>
<script>
const quantity = document.getElementById('quantity');
const button = document.getElementById('calculate');
const total = document.getElementById('total');
const status = document.getElementById('status');
window.appReady = webFront.ready.then(() => {
    button.disabled = false;
    button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
        button.disabled = true;
        status.textContent = 'Calculating';
        total.textContent = '';
        try {
            const count = Number(quantity.value);
            if (!Number.isInteger(count) || count < 1 || count > 1000)
                throw new Error('Quantity must be between 1 and 1000');
            total.textContent = String(await webFront.cppFunction('quote.calculate')(count));
            status.textContent = 'Ready';
        } catch (error) {
            status.textContent = 'Error: ' + error.message;
        } finally { button.disabled = false; }
    });
});
window.appReady.catch(error => { status.textContent = 'Error: ' + error.message; });
</script></html>

Writing the journey test

Create tests/ui/quote.spec.js. The first case enters three units, activates the button and checks that the displayed total is 75. The second enters an invalid quantity and checks for an error.

The C++ calculation is not mocked. The first case therefore exercises the click handler, bridge, C++ callback and display update. Waiting ends when the button becomes available again, with a two-second limit.

The events generated by this test are synthetic. They do not check pixel layout, native input devices or every accessibility property. React-controlled fields also require an appropriate input method.

JAVASCRIPT / JASMINE
// tests/ui/quote.spec.js — classic JavaScript, loaded into the real page.
describe('quotation journey', () => {
    beforeAll(async () => { await window.appReady; });
    const element = id => document.getElementById(id);
    function until(predicate) {
        if (predicate()) return Promise.resolve();
        return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
            const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
                if (predicate()) { cleanup(); resolve(); }
            });
            const timer = setTimeout(() => {
                cleanup(); reject(new Error('UI did not settle within 2 seconds'));
            }, 2000);
            function cleanup() { clearTimeout(timer); observer.disconnect(); }
            observer.observe(document.body, {
                subtree: true, childList: true, characterData: true, attributes: true
            });
        });
    }
    it('enters a quantity and displays the C++ price', async () => {
        element('quantity').value = '3';
        element('quantity').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}));
        element('calculate').click();
        await until(() => !element('calculate').disabled);
        expect(element('status').textContent).toBe('Ready');
        expect(element('total').textContent).toBe('75');
    });
    it('shows an error for an invalid quantity', async () => {
        element('quantity').value = '0';
        element('calculate').click();
        await until(() => !element('calculate').disabled);
        expect(element('status').textContent).toContain('Error:');
        expect(element('total').textContent).toBe('');
    });
});

Preparing the C++ application

The following main.cpp uses WKWebView and requires macOS 13.3 or later. Port 0 lets the operating system choose an available port. The document root ui is relative to the working directory set in CMake.

The JasmineTest object must exist before show is called. After the window closes, shutdown drains operations and exitCode() provides the status to return.

The CMake helper defines WEBFRONT_JASMINE_TESTING on this target. Without that macro, JasmineTest is inert. Keep a distribution target separate from the instrumented target.

C++23
#include <webfront/WebFront.hpp>
#include <webfront/testing/Jasmine.hpp>
#include <stdexcept>

using App = webfront::WebFrontWithFrontend<webfront::frontend::WKWebViewFrontend>;

int main() {
    App app{{.port = "0", .documentRoot = "ui"}};
    app.cppFunction("quote.calculate", [](int count) {
        if (count < 1 || count > 1000)
            throw std::invalid_argument("Invalid quantity");
        return count * 25;
    });
    webfront::testing::JasmineTest tests{app};
    app.show();
    app.shutdown();
    return tests.exitCode();
}

Registering the test in CMake

Place the WebFront 0.7.0 checkout in the WebFront/ subdirectory. Put main.cpp and the following CMakeLists.txt at the project root; retain the page and test paths given above.

The FRONTEND argument checks that the requested engine is enabled. The C++ programme also selects that engine explicitly. At configuration time, the helper downloads and verifies jasmine-core 7.0.2.

Specification files are classic JavaScript scripts. If their sources use TypeScript or modules, compile them beforehand.

CMAKE
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.31)
project(Quote LANGUAGES CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(WEBFRONT_EMBED_WKWEBVIEW ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
add_subdirectory(WebFront)
enable_testing()
add_executable(Quote main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(Quote PRIVATE WebFront::WebFront)
webfront_use_native_window(Quote)
webfront_add_jasmine_test(NAME QuoteJourney TARGET Quote
    SPECS tests/ui/quote.spec.js FRONTEND WKWebView TIMEOUT 60)
set_tests_properties(QuoteJourney PROPERTIES
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}")

Running the test and interpreting its result

Build the application and run CTest with the following commands. The test’s JSON report is written under build/webfront-jasmine/QuoteJourney/.

The test fails on a false assertion, a focused suite, zero executed specifications, a missing report, an application error or a timeout. Check this by replacing 75 with 74, then restore the test.

On Linux, choose CEF or WebKitGTK and install xvfb-run. On Windows, choose WebView2. The system browser is unsuitable for this testing mode. Once dependencies are provisioned, execution needs no public network access.

SYSTEM TERMINAL
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

Choosing further journeys

A useful journey test starts from a known state and checks an observable result. In Life, it might select a pattern, advance one generation, check the grid and reset the simulation. In a settings tool, it might change a value, save it, reload the page and check persistence.

Each case should establish its initial conditions and wait for a defined completion signal. Give C++ errors and disconnections separate cases. Keyboard input, focus, native dialogues and presentation require additional checks.
